content.title: E-Bikes and Unique Vehicles
content.summary: In Arvada, only legally registered motor vehicles and certain electric-assisted bicycles (e-bikes) are permitted on public roads, while off-highway and toy vehicles are prohibited. E-bikes must have pedals and a motor of 750 watts or less, adhering to specific regulations based on their class, while electric scooters and low-powered scooters have their own guidelines. Low-speed electric vehicles are allowed on streets with speed limits of 35 mph or less, provided they are registered and insured.
content.body:
## Understanding Unique or Unusual Vehicles in Arvada

Not every vehicle you see on the street is legal to drive there. Laws can be confusing, especially as new vehicles come out faster than the laws change. Here’s what you need to know.

### The Basics

Many unusual vehicles fall into one of two categories: off-highway vehicles or toy vehicles. Neither of these types are allowed on public roads, sidewalks, trails, or in parks.

Only legally registered motor vehicles and certain electric-assisted bicycles (e-bikes) are legal on public roads. Some gray areas exist in the law, which is why the purpose and design of a vehicle matter most.

### What’s Allowed?

✅ Motor Vehicles

- Cars, trucks, and motorcycles built for highways.
- Must be registered, insured, and driven by licensed drivers.
- [Colorado Revised Statutes 42-1-102 (58)(a)](https://advance.lexis.com/documentpage/?pdmfid=1000516&crid=b9a1b377-691a-49c2-8393-e8d96db67c70&config=014FJAAyNGJkY2Y4Zi1mNjgyLTRkN2YtYmE4OS03NTYzNzYzOTg0OGEKAFBvZENhdGFsb2d592qv2Kywlf8caKqYROP5&pddocfullpath=%252Fshared%252Fdocument%252Fstatutes-legislation%252Furn%253AcontentItem%253A6G00-6D03-RRKN-206C-00008-00&pdcontentcomponentid=234176&pdteaserkey=sr0&pditab=allpods&ecomp=6s65kkk&earg=sr0&prid=f04c9eba-15d5-455e-96eb-04add40dc6f3)

✅ Electric-Assisted Bicycles (E-Bikes)

- Have pedals and a 750 watt (or less) electric motor.
- Must follow rules of the road for bicycles.
- [Colorado Revised Statutes 42-1-102 (28.5)](https://advance.lexis.com/documentpage/?pdmfid=1000516&crid=b9a1b377-691a-49c2-8393-e8d96db67c70&config=014FJAAyNGJkY2Y4Zi1mNjgyLTRkN2YtYmE4OS03NTYzNzYzOTg0OGEKAFBvZENhdGFsb2d592qv2Kywlf8caKqYROP5&pddocfullpath=%252Fshared%252Fdocument%252Fstatutes-legislation%252Furn%253AcontentItem%253A6G00-6D03-RRKN-206C-00008-00&pdcontentcomponentid=234176&pdteaserkey=sr0&pditab=allpods&ecomp=6s65kkk&earg=sr0&prid=f04c9eba-15d5-455e-96eb-04add40dc6f3)

Three types:

- Class 1 & 2: Motor assist up to 20 mph. Allowed on roads, sidewalks, trails, and in parks (15 mph speed limit in parks).
- Class 3: Motor assist up to 28 mph. Riders must be 16+. Helmets required under 18. Not allowed on sidewalks, trails, or in parks.

✅ Electric Scooter

- Has handlebars and weighs less than 100lbs.
- Powered by an electric motor with a maximum speed of 20mph.
- Allowed on roads, sidewalks, trails, and in parks (15 mph speed limit in parks).
- Must follow rules of the road for bicycles.

✅ Low-Powered Scooters

- Small scooters with engines under 50cc or 4,476 watts.
- Must be registered, insured, and driven by licensed drivers.
- Helmets required under 18. Eye protection required.
- Not allowed on sidewalks, trails, or in parks.
- [Colorado Revised Statutes 42-1-102 (48)(48.5)(a)](https://advance.lexis.com/documentpage/?pdmfid=1000516&crid=b9a1b377-691a-49c2-8393-e8d96db67c70&config=014FJAAyNGJkY2Y4Zi1mNjgyLTRkN2YtYmE4OS03NTYzNzYzOTg0OGEKAFBvZENhdGFsb2d592qv2Kywlf8caKqYROP5&pddocfullpath=%252Fshared%252Fdocument%252Fstatutes-legislation%252Furn%253AcontentItem%253A6G00-6D03-RRKN-206C-00008-00&pdcontentcomponentid=234176&pdteaserkey=sr0&pditab=allpods&ecomp=6s65kkk&earg=sr0&prid=f04c9eba-15d5-455e-96eb-04add40dc6f3)

✅ Low-Speed Electric Vehicles (LSEVs)

- Look like small cars and are electric.
- Allowed on streets with speed limits of 35 mph or less.
- Must be registered, insured, and driven by licensed drivers.
- [Colorado Revised Statutes 42-1-102 (48)(48.6)](https://advance.lexis.com/documentpage/?pdmfid=1000516&crid=b9a1b377-691a-49c2-8393-e8d96db67c70&config=014FJAAyNGJkY2Y4Zi1mNjgyLTRkN2YtYmE4OS03NTYzNzYzOTg0OGEKAFBvZENhdGFsb2d592qv2Kywlf8caKqYROP5&pddocfullpath=%252Fshared%252Fdocument%252Fstatutes-legislation%252Furn%253AcontentItem%253A6G00-6D03-RRKN-206C-00008-00&pdcontentcomponentid=234176&pdteaserkey=sr0&pditab=allpods&ecomp=6s65kkk&earg=sr0&prid=f04c9eba-15d5-455e-96eb-04add40dc6f3)

### What’s NOT Allowed?

❌ Off-Highway Vehicles

- Designed for dirt, not pavement (dirt bikes, ATVs, side by sides).
- Illegal on roads, trails, sidewalks, and in parks.
- Dirt bikes may be “street legal” if fully registered, equipped, and operated per law.
- [Colorado Revised Statutes 33-14.5-101 (3)](https://advance.lexis.com/documentpage/?pdmfid=1000516&crid=2d5f8bd9-8745-4209-b706-6ce9c45a2af0&config=014FJAAyNGJkY2Y4Zi1mNjgyLTRkN2YtYmE4OS03NTYzNzYzOTg0OGEKAFBvZENhdGFsb2d592qv2Kywlf8caKqYROP5&pddocfullpath=%252Fshared%252Fdocument%252Fstatutes-legislation%252Furn%253AcontentItem%253A61P5-WXH1-DYDC-J134-00008-00&pdcontentcomponentid=234176&pdteaserkey=sr0&pditab=allpods&ecomp=6s65kkk&earg=sr0&prid=4d0819f3-787b-4b5b-82be-ef0193ac51ab)

❌ Toy Vehicles

- Vehicles not designed for road or off-road use (minibikes, pocket bikes, Go-Peds).
- Illegal on roads, trails, sidewalks, and in parks.
- [Colorado Revised Statutes 42-1-102 (103.5)(a)](https://advance.lexis.com/documentpage/?pdmfid=1000516&crid=b9a1b377-691a-49c2-8393-e8d96db67c70&config=014FJAAyNGJkY2Y4Zi1mNjgyLTRkN2YtYmE4OS03NTYzNzYzOTg0OGEKAFBvZENhdGFsb2d592qv2Kywlf8caKqYROP5&pddocfullpath=%252Fshared%252Fdocument%252Fstatutes-legislation%252Furn%253AcontentItem%253A6G00-6D03-RRKN-206C-00008-00&pdcontentcomponentid=234176&pdteaserkey=sr0&pditab=allpods&ecomp=6s65kkk&earg=sr0&prid=f04c9eba-15d5-455e-96eb-04add40dc6f3)

❌ Golf Carts

- Illegal on roads, trails, sidewalks, and in parks.
- [Colorado Revised Statutes 42-1-102 (39.5)](https://advance.lexis.com/documentpage/?pdmfid=1000516&crid=b9a1b377-691a-49c2-8393-e8d96db67c70&config=014FJAAyNGJkY2Y4Zi1mNjgyLTRkN2YtYmE4OS03NTYzNzYzOTg0OGEKAFBvZENhdGFsb2d592qv2Kywlf8caKqYROP5&pddocfullpath=%252Fshared%252Fdocument%252Fstatutes-legislation%252Furn%253AcontentItem%253A6G00-6D03-RRKN-206C-00008-00&pdcontentcomponentid=234176&pdteaserkey=sr0&pditab=allpods&ecomp=6s65kkk&earg=sr0&prid=f04c9eba-15d5-455e-96eb-04add40dc6f3)

❌ Other High-Power Electric Vehicles

- Oversized e-bikes or scooters may be considered motorcycles if their power exceeds 4,476 watts.
- Illegal on roads, trails, sidewalks, and in parks.
- May be “street legal” if fully registered, equipped, and operated per law.

### Quick Reminder

If it was designed to be used on public roads and has the proper registration and safety equipment, it’s probably legal. If it looks like a toy, dirt bike, or off-road vehicle, it’s probably not legal.

Always check City ordinances and State law before buying or using a unique vehicle on the streets.
